Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear questionnaire. Quick answers below; attaching a concise write-up (redwood-slo-answers.pdf) and I can set a 30-min call if you'd like to walk through.

1) Availability & p99 latency:
- Availability: measured as the percentage of successful 2xx responses over total requests to the selected production endpoints; default evaluation window is 30 days for monthly SLOs, and 7 days for short-term health checks.
- p99 latency: computed from end-to-end request latency distribution at the edge for completed requests (5xx excluded). We use a rolling 7-day and 30-day percentile evaluation by default; SLA commitments reference the 30-day window.

2) Alerting thresholds:
- Default: page when 5xx rate exceeds 0.5% sustained for 5m for production routes, and when p99 latency exceeds configured threshold (route-dependent) for 10m.
- Custom policies: yes — we support tenant-scoped alert rules and can onboard custom thresholds via our onboarding playbook.

3) Read-only dashboard access:
- We can provide a Grafana read-only view scoped to your tenant plus a curated uptime/latency dashboard. Auth is via a short-lived API token or SSO (SAML) depending on your preference.
- Metrics retention: aggregated metrics (time series) retained for 90 days by default; high-cardinality request logs retained 30 days in hosted mode unless you contract extended retention.

4) Exception process:
- Exceptions (e.g., altered retention, bespoke SLOs) require a product/engineering review and legal sign-off. Typical turn-around: 7–14 business days for routine exceptions; longer if infra changes required. Any exception is documented as an addendum to the contract.

5) Data retention specifics:
- Metrics TS: 90 days; fine-grained request traces/logs: 30 days. We can arrange longer retention on Dedicated or Private deployments (we've done 1yr+ for enterprise customers).

Next steps: can we pencil a call on Wed 20 May 10:00am PT? If that works, I'll add our SRE (Marissa) to cover the telemetry details.

+1 on the proposed replies. A few clarifications / nitty-gritty you can paste back to OliveTech: 

- Grafana access: we can create a tenant-scoped read-only Grafana API key with time-bounded validity. Security notes: keys are bearer tokens — recommend 90-day max unless they require SAML. We log token creations and provide rotation guidance. If they require external auditors, we can issue a service-account style token and a one-time export of the dashboard to PDF for audit windows.

- Retention: hosted default is 90d for aggregated TS metrics (prom-style), 30d for raw request/trace logs. For Dedicated or Private we offer configurable retention (30d—365d+). If OliveTech wants longer retention on hosted, we need a retention-addendum.

- Measurement & windows: availability is measured per-route using success ratio (2xx / total) with sampling at the edge. We compute p99 using raw latencies after outlier trimming of client-side aborted requests. For SLA language, use: "Availability measured monthly (30d rolling) with a p99 latency evaluated on a 30d rolling window. Incidents are counted when service error rate exceeds X for Y minutes." 

- Exception precedent: typical exceptions we've granted include extended metrics retention and custom alert thresholds. Those were processed as an SLO addendum and required a one-time infra ticket and legal sign-off. Typical timeline 7–21 business days.

I've attached a CSV matrix that maps common SLO questions to the evidence we can produce. Feel free to redact any infra-internal notes before sending.

Marissa
SRE, Platform Observability
Redwood Inference
